Severity is derived from the Wazuh rule level: **low** 0-6, **medium** 7-11, **high** 12-14, **critical** 15.

## Detection details

### SOC-AUTH-001 — SSH authentication failure (rule 100100)

* **Description:** A single failed SSH password/public-key login or an attempt for a non-existent user.
* **Severity:** low (Wazuh level 5)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sshd) - lab-linux-01:/var/log/lab/auth.log
* **Detection logic:** Child of any stock sshd rule (if_group sshd) whose message contains "Failed password", "Failed publickey", "Invalid user" or "authentication failure".
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110.001 Brute Force: Password Guessing (Credential Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Users mistyping passwords; expired credentials in scripts. Low severity by design - it feeds the correlation rules.
* **Recommended response:** No action on a single event; review if it repeats for one account or source. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_ssh_bruteforce
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.205 s

### SOC-AUTH-002 — SSH brute force (rule 100101)

* **Description:** Five or more SSH authentication failures from the same source IP within 120 seconds.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sshd)
* **Detection logic:** frequency=5, timeframe=120s, if_matched_sid 100100, same_srcip.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110.001 Brute Force: Password Guessing (Credential Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Misconfigured automation retrying with an old password; vulnerability scanners run by the security team.
* **Recommended response:** Identify targeted accounts, check for any success from the source (SOC-AUTH-003), block the source at the perimeter, enforce key-only SSH. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_ssh_bruteforce, auth_ssh_success_after_failures
* **False-positive test:** neg_ssh_single_failure
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.238 s

### SOC-AUTH-003 — SSH login after brute force (rule 100102)

* **Description:** A successful SSH login from a source that triggered the brute-force rule in the previous 10 minutes.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 13)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sshd)
* **Detection logic:** if_group sshd + "Accepted ..." message, if_matched_sid 100101, same_srcip, timeframe=600s.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110 Brute Force (Credential Access); T1078 Valid Accounts (Initial Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** A legitimate user who mistyped several times and then succeeded from the same IP. Confirm with the user out-of-band.
* **Recommended response:** Treat as account compromise until disproven - disable the account, kill sessions, review commands executed, rotate credentials. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_ssh_success_after_failures
* **False-positive test:** neg_ssh_single_failure
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.238 s

### SOC-AUTH-004 — Windows logon failure (rule 100110)

* **Description:** Windows Security event 4625 (an account failed to log on).
* **Severity:** low (Wazuh level 5)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log (EventChannel) - lab-win-01
* **Detection logic:** if_group windows, channel Security, eventID 4625.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110 Brute Force (Credential Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Mistyped passwords, stale mapped-drive credentials, services with expired passwords.
* **Recommended response:** Informational; feeds SOC-AUTH-005. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_windows_logon_failures
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.356 s

### SOC-AUTH-005 — Multiple Windows logon failures (rule 100111)

* **Description:** Four or more 4625 failures from the same source IP within 120 seconds.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log
* **Detection logic:** frequency=4, timeframe=120s, if_matched_sid 100110, same_field win.eventdata.ipAddress.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110 Brute Force (Credential Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Service account with a changed password still configured on a server; account lockout tests.
* **Recommended response:** Identify target accounts and logon type, check lockouts and any later 4624 from the same IP, block the source. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_windows_logon_failures, auth_windows_success_after_failures
* **False-positive test:** neg_windows_single_logon_failure
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.374 s

### SOC-AUTH-006 — Windows logon after repeated failures (rule 100112)

* **Description:** A successful Windows logon (4624) from a source that triggered SOC-AUTH-005 within 10 minutes.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 13)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log
* **Detection logic:** eventID 4624, if_matched_sid 100111, same_field win.eventdata.ipAddress, timeframe=600s.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1110 Brute Force (Credential Access); T1078 Valid Accounts (Initial Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** User succeeding after several typos from their own workstation.
* **Recommended response:** Treat as compromised credentials - disable/reset the account, review the session (4624 LogonId) and subsequent process creation. → playbook `IR-001`
* **True-positive test:** auth_windows_success_after_failures
* **False-positive test:** neg_windows_single_logon_failure
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.381 s

### SOC-PRIV-001 — Root shell via sudo (rule 100120)

* **Description:** A user runs an interactive shell (bash/sh/zsh/su) as root through sudo.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sudo)
* **Detection logic:** if_group sudo, "USER=root", command matches a shell or su binary.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching (Privilege Escalation)
* **False-positive considerations:** Administrators using `sudo -i` / `sudo su -` for maintenance. Tune with an allow-list of admin accounts.
* **Recommended response:** Confirm the user is an authorised administrator and a change ticket exists; otherwise review the session and revoke sudo rights. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** priv_sudo_root_shell
* **False-positive test:** neg_sudo_routine_admin
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.247 s

### SOC-PRIV-002 — Repeated unauthorized sudo (rule 100121)

* **Description:** A user who is not in sudoers attempts sudo three or more times within 5 minutes.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sudo)
* **Detection logic:** frequency=3, timeframe=300s, if_matched_sid 5405 (user NOT in sudoers), same_srcuser.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching (Privilege Escalation)
* **False-positive considerations:** New staff whose sudo access has not been provisioned yet.
* **Recommended response:** Contact the user and their manager; if unexplained, treat the account as compromised and review what it attempted to run. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** priv_unauthorized_sudo_repeated
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.288 s

### SOC-PRIV-003 — SUID/SGID bit set (rule 100122)

* **Description:** auditd records chmod setting the setuid/setgid bit (u+s, g+s, 4755, ...).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Linux audit log (EXECVE) - lab-linux-01:/var/log/lab/audit.log
* **Detection logic:** if_group audit, audit.command chmod, EXECVE argument matching a +s symbolic mode or a 2xxx-7xxx octal mode.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1548.001 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid (Privilege Escalation)
* **False-positive considerations:** Package installation scripts (normally run by dpkg/rpm, not interactively); deliberate admin changes.
* **Recommended response:** Identify the file, revert the mode, check file integrity and who (auid) ran the command; hunt for other SUID changes. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** priv_setuid_chmod
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.247 s

### SOC-PERS-001 — Linux account added to privileged group (rule 100180)

* **Description:** usermod adds an account to sudo, wheel, admin, adm, root, docker or lxd.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (usermod) - custom decoder soc-usermod
* **Detection logic:** decoded_as soc-usermod, group field in the privileged-group list.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1098 Account Manipulation (Persistence); T1136.001 Create Account: Local Account (Persistence)
* **False-positive considerations:** Onboarding of a new administrator through a change request.
* **Recommended response:** Verify against the change/onboarding record; if unapproved remove the membership, lock the account and investigate who ran usermod. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** persist_linux_user_added_to_sudo
* **False-positive test:** neg_linux_user_regular_group
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.248 s

### SOC-PERS-002 — Windows account added to privileged group (rule 100182)

* **Description:** A member is added to BUILTIN\Administrators or Domain/Enterprise/Schema Admins (4732/4728/4756).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log
* **Detection logic:** eventID 4732|4728|4756 and targetSid S-1-5-32-544 or a RID 512/518/519 group.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1098 Account Manipulation (Persistence)
* **False-positive considerations:** Approved administrator onboarding.
* **Recommended response:** Validate with the change record; otherwise remove the membership, disable the added account, investigate the subject account. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** persist_windows_admin_account
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.396 s

### SOC-PERS-003 — New Windows local account (rule 100183)

* **Description:** Windows Security event 4720 (a user account was created).
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 8)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log
* **Detection logic:** eventID 4720 on the Security channel.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1136.001 Create Account: Local Account (Persistence)
* **False-positive considerations:** Normal provisioning by IT.
* **Recommended response:** Confirm the account is expected; correlate with SOC-PERS-002 for privilege grants. → playbook `IR-002`
* **True-positive test:** persist_windows_admin_account
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.396 s

### SOC-PS-001 — PowerShell download cradle (rule 100130)

* **Description:** Script block logging shows IEX/Invoke-Expression combined with a download primitive (Net.WebClient, Invoke-WebRequest, ...).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational 4104 (script block logging)
* **Detection logic:** if_group powershell, eventID 4104, scriptBlockText contains both an execution (IEX) and a download primitive.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell (Execution); T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer (Command and Control)
* **False-positive considerations:** Installers that bootstrap with `iex (irm ...)` (e.g. package managers). Allow-list known URLs.
* **Recommended response:** Retrieve the full script block and URL, block the domain/IP, isolate the host if the payload executed, collect the downloaded content. → playbook `IR-004`
* **True-positive test:** powershell_download_cradle
* **False-positive test:** neg_powershell_scriptblock_benign
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.401 s

### SOC-PS-002 — Hidden / encoded PowerShell (rule 100131)

* **Description:** powershell.exe started with an encoded command and/or a hidden window (Sysmon event 1).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational event 1 (process creation)
* **Detection logic:** Sysmon EID 1, image powershell.exe/pwsh.exe, command line with -e/-enc/-EncodedCommand <base64> or -w hidden.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell (Execution); T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** Some management agents (SCCM, RMM tools) launch encoded PowerShell. Allow-list by parent image and signer.
* **Recommended response:** Decode the command (base64 UTF-16LE), review parent process and user, isolate if malicious. → playbook `IR-004`
* **True-positive test:** powershell_encoded_hidden
* **False-positive test:** neg_powershell_process_benign
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.401 s

### SOC-PS-003 — PowerShell Defender/AMSI tampering (rule 100132)

* **Description:** Script block disables Defender protections, adds exclusions or references AMSI bypass primitives.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 14)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational 4104
* **Detection logic:** eventID 4104, scriptBlockText matches Set-MpPreference -Disable*, Add-MpPreference -Exclusion*, AmsiUtils or amsiInitFailed.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1562.001 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Evasion); T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** Very rare; possible during sanctioned AV troubleshooting.
* **Recommended response:** Re-enable protection, isolate the host, investigate what ran after protections were disabled. → playbook `IR-007`
* **True-positive test:** powershell_defender_tamper
* **False-positive test:** neg_powershell_scriptblock_benign
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.402 s

### SOC-PROC-001 — LOLBin file download (rule 100140)

* **Description:** certutil or bitsadmin used to download a remote file (Sysmon event 1).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational event 1
* **Detection logic:** image certutil.exe/bitsadmin.exe and command line with -urlcache, -verifyctl, /transfer or /addfile.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer (Command and Control); T1218 System Binary Proxy Execution (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** Rare legitimate certificate-cache maintenance by admins.
* **Recommended response:** Identify the URL and destination file, quarantine and hash the file, block the URL, check for execution of the file. → playbook `IR-006`
* **True-positive test:** process_certutil_download
* **False-positive test:** neg_certutil_hashfile, neg_process_notepad
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.404 s

### SOC-PROC-002 — Office spawns shell (rule 100141)

* **Description:** A Microsoft Office application starts cmd, PowerShell, a script host, mshta, rundll32 or regsvr32.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational event 1
* **Detection logic:** parentImage winword/excel/powerpnt/outlook/msaccess/mspub/onenote and image in the shell/LOLBin list.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1204.002 User Execution: Malicious File (Execution); T1059.003 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** Legacy macros used by business processes. Inventory and sign them.
* **Recommended response:** Retrieve the document, isolate the host, review child process tree and network connections, notify the user. → playbook `IR-006`
* **True-positive test:** process_office_spawns_shell
* **False-positive test:** neg_process_notepad, neg_powershell_process_benign
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.404 s

### SOC-PROC-003 — Netcat reverse/bind shell (rule 100142)

* **Description:** auditd records netcat executed with -e or -c (spawn a program on connect).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Linux audit log (EXECVE)
* **Detection logic:** audit.command nc/ncat/netcat and an EXECVE argument -e/-c.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** Almost none on servers; possible in admin troubleshooting labs.
* **Recommended response:** Kill the process, isolate the host, identify the parent (often a web server account), look for the initial exploit. → playbook `IR-006`
* **True-positive test:** process_linux_netcat_shell
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.287 s

### SOC-NET-001 — Network scan signature (rule 100150)

* **Description:** Suricata raised an "ET SCAN" signature.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 8)
* **Data source:** Suricata EVE JSON (lab-nids-01:/var/log/lab/suricata/eve.json)
* **Detection logic:** if_group suricata, event_type alert, alert.signature starts with "ET SCAN ".
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1046 Network Service Discovery (Discovery)
* **False-positive considerations:** Authorised vulnerability scanners and asset-discovery tools.
* **Recommended response:** Check whether the source is an approved scanner; otherwise watch for follow-up exploitation from the same source. → playbook `IR-005`
* **True-positive test:** network_scan_suricata
* **False-positive test:** neg_suricata_policy_alert
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.121 s

### SOC-NET-002 — Port scan (correlated) (rule 100151)

* **Description:** Four or more Suricata scan alerts from the same source within 120 seconds.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Suricata EVE JSON
* **Detection logic:** frequency=4, timeframe=120s, if_matched_sid 100150, same_field src_ip.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1046 Network Service Discovery (Discovery)
* **False-positive considerations:** Scheduled authorised scans - suppress by source during approved windows.
* **Recommended response:** Identify scanned hosts/ports, block the source, verify no exposed service was exploited afterwards. → playbook `IR-005`
* **True-positive test:** network_scan_suricata
* **False-positive test:** neg_suricata_policy_alert
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.121 s

### SOC-OUT-001 — Script host outbound on non-standard port (rule 100200)

* **Description:** PowerShell or another script/LOLBin process opens an outbound connection to a public IP on a port other than 80/443/53/8080/8443.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational event 3 (network connection)
* **Detection logic:** Sysmon EID 3, initiated=true, image in the script-host list, destinationPort not standard, destinationIp not RFC1918/loopback.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1571 Non-Standard Port (Command and Control); T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** Admin scripts talking to internal-but-public-addressed services on custom ports.
* **Recommended response:** Identify the destination, block it, capture the process tree and memory, isolate the host if C2 is suspected. → playbook `IR-006`
* **True-positive test:** outbound_powershell_nonstandard_port
* **False-positive test:** neg_outbound_browser_https
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.396 s

### SOC-OUT-002 — Outbound C2 signature (rule 100201)

* **Description:** Suricata MALWARE/CNC/TROJAN signature on traffic originating from an internal host.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Suricata EVE JSON
* **Detection logic:** event_type alert, signature prefix ET MALWARE|CNC|TROJAN|ATTACK_RESPONSE, src_ip in RFC1918.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (Command and Control)
* **False-positive considerations:** Signature false positives on CDN traffic; verify the payload/JA3.
* **Recommended response:** Isolate the internal host, block the destination, collect memory and disk triage. → playbook `IR-006`
* **True-positive test:** outbound_suricata_c2
* **False-positive test:** neg_suricata_policy_alert
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.16 s

### SOC-WEB-001 — Sensitive path request (rule 100160)

* **Description:** Request for a well-known sensitive file or admin path (.env, .git, wp-admin, phpmyadmin, backups...).
* **Severity:** low (Wazuh level 6)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log (lab-web-01)
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, URL matches the sensitive-path list.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1595.003 Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning (Reconnaissance)
* **False-positive considerations:** Administrators browsing admin panels; security scanners.
* **Recommended response:** Verify the response codes - any 200 on a secret file is an exposure incident. Feeds SOC-WEB-001b. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_recon_sensitive_paths
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.215 s

### SOC-WEB-001b — Web content discovery (rule 100161)

* **Description:** Six or more sensitive-path requests from one source within 60 seconds.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** frequency=6, timeframe=60s, if_matched_sid 100160, same_srcip.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1595.003 Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning (Reconnaissance)
* **False-positive considerations:** Authorised DAST scans.
* **Recommended response:** Rate-limit/block the source, review all URLs that returned 2xx, check for secret exposure. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_recon_sensitive_paths
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.23 s

### SOC-WEB-002 — Scanner user agent (rule 100162)

* **Description:** User-Agent of a known scanner (sqlmap, nikto, nuclei, gobuster, wpscan, ...).
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 8)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, last quoted field (User-Agent) contains a scanner name.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1595.002 Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning (Reconnaissance)
* **False-positive considerations:** Internal security testing.
* **Recommended response:** Confirm whether the scan is authorised; block the source if not and review its other requests. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_scanner_user_agent
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.229 s

### SOC-WEB-003 — Path traversal / LFI (rule 100163)

* **Description:** URL tries to escape the web root or read OS files (../, %2e%2e, /etc/passwd, win.ini).
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, URL matches traversal sequences or sensitive OS file paths.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access); T1083 File and Directory Discovery (Discovery)
* **False-positive considerations:** Rare; some apps legitimately pass relative paths in parameters.
* **Recommended response:** Check the response status/size; if 200 assume file disclosure and rotate exposed secrets. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_path_traversal
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.202 s

### SOC-WEB-004 — SQL injection (rule 100170)

* **Description:** SQL injection syntax in the URL (UNION SELECT, ' OR 1=1, information_schema, sleep(), xp_cmdshell).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, URL matches SQLi patterns (raw and URL-encoded).
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Search boxes containing SQL keywords; developer tooling.
* **Recommended response:** Check the application/database logs for errors or data returned, block the source, patch the vulnerable parameter. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_sql_injection
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.229 s

### SOC-WEB-005 — Cross-site scripting (rule 100171)

* **Description:** XSS payloads in the URL (<script>, javascript:, onerror=, document.cookie).
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, URL matches XSS patterns (raw and URL-encoded).
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access); T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** CMS editors posting HTML; marketing tracking parameters.
* **Recommended response:** Verify output encoding on the affected page, check whether the payload is stored, block the source. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_xss
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.23 s

### SOC-WEB-006 — OS command injection (rule 100172)

* **Description:** Shell metacharacters followed by a command (;cat, |id, $(whoami), `uname`) in the URL.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, URL matches separator + common command.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access); T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution)
* **False-positive considerations:** Very rare in normal traffic.
* **Recommended response:** Check for spawned processes on the web host (auditd), isolate if executed, patch the endpoint. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_command_injection
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.202 s

### SOC-WEB-007 — Log4Shell JNDI injection (rule 100173)

* **Description:** ${jndi:...} lookup strings (including common obfuscations) anywhere in the request line or User-Agent.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 14)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, full log matches ${jndi: / ${${lower:j} / ${${::-j}.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access)
* **False-positive considerations:** Security scanners checking for CVE-2021-44228.
* **Recommended response:** Verify no Java service behind the proxy is vulnerable, look for outbound LDAP/RMI from servers, block the callback host. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_log4shell_jndi
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.201 s

### SOC-WEB-008 — Unusual HTTP method (rule 100164)

* **Description:** TRACE, TRACK, DEBUG, WebDAV or CONNECT methods against the web server.
* **Severity:** low (Wazuh level 5)
* **Data source:** Nginx access log
* **Detection logic:** if_group accesslog, decoded HTTP method in the unusual-method list.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1595.002 Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning (Reconnaissance)
* **False-positive considerations:** WebDAV clients where WebDAV is in use.
* **Recommended response:** Low priority; correlate with other activity from the same source. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_unusual_http_method
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.23 s

### SOC-WEB-009 — Blocked hidden-file access (Nginx error log) (rule 100175)

* **Description:** Nginx error log reports "access forbidden by rule" for .git/.env/.svn/.htpasswd/.aws/.ssh.
* **Severity:** low (Wazuh level 6)
* **Data source:** Nginx error log (lab-web-01)
* **Detection logic:** if_group nginx, message "access forbidden by rule", request path is a hidden secret/repository file.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1595.003 Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning (Reconnaissance)
* **False-positive considerations:** Developers testing deny rules.
* **Recommended response:** Confirms the deny rule works; correlate with SOC-WEB-001 for the same source. → playbook `IR-003`
* **True-positive test:** web_forbidden_hidden_file
* **False-positive test:** neg_web_normal_browsing
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.202 s

### SOC-CONF-001 — Windows event log cleared (rule 100190)

* **Description:** Security log cleared (1102) or System log cleared (104).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Windows Security/System event log
* **Detection logic:** provider Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog, eventID 1102 or 104.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1070.001 Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** Rare, documented maintenance.
* **Recommended response:** Rely on forwarded copies in the SIEM, identify the subject account, investigate activity before the clear. → playbook `IR-007`
* **True-positive test:** config_windows_log_cleared
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.385 s

### SOC-CONF-002 — Windows audit policy weakened (rule 100191)

* **Description:** Event 4719 where success or failure auditing was removed.
* **Severity:** medium (Wazuh level 10)
* **Data source:** Windows Security event log
* **Detection logic:** eventID 4719 and auditPolicyChanges "removed" (%%8448 / %%8450).
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1562.002 Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** GPO changes rolled out by administrators.
* **Recommended response:** Compare with GPO change records, restore the audit policy, review the subject account. → playbook `IR-007`
* **True-positive test:** config_windows_audit_policy_change
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.379 s

### SOC-CONF-003 — Defender protection disabled (rule 100192)

* **Description:** Microsoft Defender reports real-time protection or scanning disabled (5001/5010/5012).
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational
* **Detection logic:** Defender channel, eventID 5001|5010|5012.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1562.001 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** Third-party AV taking over; sanctioned troubleshooting.
* **Recommended response:** Re-enable protection, find the process/user that changed it, scan the host. → playbook `IR-007`
* **True-positive test:** config_defender_realtime_disabled
* **False-positive test:** none (no benign variant of this event type)
* **Measured detection latency:** 0.38 s

### SOC-CONF-004 — Linux security control disabled (rule 100193)

* **Description:** sudo used to disable the firewall, SELinux, auditd, AppArmor, rsyslog, Suricata or the Wazuh agent.
* **Severity:** high (Wazuh level 12)
* **Data source:** Linux auth log (sudo)
* **Detection logic:** if_group sudo, command matches ufw disable, setenforce 0, iptables -F, auditctl -D/-e 0, systemctl stop|disable|mask <security service>.
* **MITRE ATT&CK:** T1562.001 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Evasion); T1562.004 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify System Firewall (Defense Evasion)
* **False-positive considerations:** Planned maintenance windows.
* **Recommended response:** Re-enable the control, confirm a change ticket, review commands run while the control was off. → playbook `IR-007`
* **True-positive test:** config_linux_security_disabled
* **False-positive test:** neg_sudo_routine_admin
* **Measured detection latency:** 1.235 s
